long_biography.plain_text:
Abt learned the business from the workshop floor, training as a freight-forwarding clerk and motor mechanic before joining the family enterprise. In 1991 he took over its tuning division and helped establish ABT Sportsline as a separate company. He expanded the operation beyond Germany through subsidiaries and an export network serving Volkswagen Group vehicles.

Motorsport remained the development laboratory and public face of that growth. Abt raced in Volkswagen one-make competition, then concentrated on team leadership, guiding privateer and factory programmes in touring cars. He also backed ABT's early entry into Formula E and later electric-road projects. Today he is the ABT Group's chief executive and ABT Sportsline's managing shareholder, while other family members and executives hold distinct operating responsibilities.

proposed_details.existing_value:
The delivery of the Benetti Oasis 40M yacht named Oreos took place in May 2023. The yacht was sold to its current owner in late 2020, and its construction began specifically for the buyer. At the time of the sale, the base price for the yacht model was €19,400,000. Representing the buyer was Kurt Lehmann from Yacht Moments.

According to the classification society RINA, the yacht is registered under the ownership of a Maltese company called Oreos Yachting Limited. The shareholders of the owning company are Hans-Jürgen Abt, who holds 80% of the shares, and El Atun LLC, a Delaware-based company in the United States, which owns the remaining 20% of the shares. Serving as the director and judicial and legal representative of Oreos Yachting Limited is Matty Zadnikar from Seanet.

Hans-Jürgen Abt is a German entrepreneur and former racing driver. In 1991, he founded the ABT Sportsline group of companies, which currently employs over 180 people. The company specializes in power boosts, aerodynamic packages, alloy wheels, suspensions, brakes, and customized interior conversions for vehicles from VW, Audi, Seat, and Skoda.

Previously, Hans-Jürgen Abt owned the Custom Line Navetta 33 yacht named Christina A, which is now known as Mac One. Kurt Lehmann from Yacht Moments sold this yacht on his behalf in March 2022.

In May 2023, the yacht Oreos was listed for sale by SeaNet Europe Ltd, offering a 33.33% co-ownership opportunity. It is important to note that the shareholder list of Oreos Yachting Limited suggests that the yacht already has a co-owner, possibly a US national, although Delaware companies have been utilized by individuals from various nationalities in the past.

uncertainties.detail: The legal chain is current and specific: the owner input links Hans-Jürgen Abt to Oreos; a registry-derived company record separately names Hans and Christopher Kernon as Oreos Yachting Limited shareholders; and the U.S. Coast Guard identifies that company as Oreos's owner. Public sources do not disclose a definitive current personal percentage. This dossier therefore confirms association but does not repeat the upstream 80% claim or YachtAhoy's conflicting 33% figure.

Kernon is a separately named shareholder and separately researched owner. No occupation, nationality, residence, ownership percentage, family relationship or wealth fact is transferred between him and Abt. The joint legal-company association is used only to explain why both records connect to Oreos.

Johann Abt built the prior-generation tuning and motorsport platform; Christian Abt initially co-led Sportsline and has separate racing results; Daniel Abt has separate driving and marketing roles. Hans-Jürgen's dossier uses only facts expressly attributed to him, while family history is included only to explain the inherited platform.

Hans-Jürgen founded the ABT Sportsline corporate entity and expanded it internationally, but official history also says he took over the parental tuning division. Because the material operating platform was transferred rather than independently started, Inherited and expanded is more precise than Self-made — advantaged start.

ABT participates in motorsport and electric projects, but the current group role and product base remain automotive. Motorsport is a defining sporting and development identity rather than a better broad wealth-industry classification.

The existing biography is dominated by vessel delivery, price, ownership percentages, sale history and speculation about co-owner nationality. Those details are volatile, partly conflicting and not a durable portrait. The proposed replacement preserves the supported automotive identity and removes all Oreos sale and share commentary.
